D-JCC25.title: Journals of the Continental Congress, 1774–1789, vol. 25 (Library of Congress, 1922), archive.org OCR

episode.outcome: After Washington handed over his commission and a copy of his address, he resumed his place and the President delivered Congress's answer. The answer opens by saying Congress receives the resignation 'with emotions, too affecting for utterance' and closes with a prayer for him. The journal then moves on to December 24.
episode.quote: He then advanced and delivered to the President his commission, with a copy of his address, and rctiu'Dcd to having resumed his place, whereupon the President return- ed him the following answer:

episode.outcome: On the December 20 vote on whether seven states were competent to receive the resignation, the roll call in the reading range shows only Partridge voting no, and Ellery's no changed to ay. The journal states no separate result, and the editors' footnote describes the entry only as the 'sense of the House taken… with yeas and nays'.
episode.quote: Sense of the House taken on the competency of seven atatea to receive the resignation of Commander in Cliief, with yeaa and nays, December 20, 1783.

additions.why: Congress's spoken reply is the direct response and the end of the audience. The piece stops at the handover and says the reply cannot be quoted, but it sits right after U-E9 in the reading range.

additions.start: We feel with you our obligations to the army in general
additions.end: reward which this world cannot give.
additions.why: The second half of the reply answers Washington's two requests point by point: Congress promises to look after his confidential officers and joins him in commending the country to God. This is the reply to the content of story.4.
Completes the roll call: Forster, Gerry and Osgood also voted ay. This shows that Partridge was the only no in the whole recorded list, not just in the portion cited.

claims.scope: Clauses 4–6 of the December 22 order of audience

quote.quote: the secretary is to deliver the General a copy of the addroaa answer, and receive the commiBoion from the General, who [and the General] is then to take his leave.

claims.fix: The garbled words ('addroaa', 'commiBoion', 'pre acntod to the Scorotaiy') appear to be struck-through words in the printed edition, but OCR alone cannot confirm this. Say: 'Some garbled words in the OCR may be deletions; this needs checking against the facsimile.'

context_issues.problem: The scene stops at the handover. Immediately afterwards the source records that Washington returned to his place and the President delivered Congress's answer. Readers are left thinking the ceremony ended with the handover, and the institution's spoken response, the other half of the episode, is missing.

quote.quote: and rctiu'Dcd to having resumed his place, whereupon the President return- ed him the following answer:

context_issues.problem: The parenthetical says the journal and clause 6 of the draft do not match on who receives the commission. But Boudinot's bracketed insertion in clause 4 already changes the procedure to the General delivering the commission and the copy of his address to the President. The revised protocol therefore matches the journal; the garbled wording of clause 6 most likely reflects the pre-revision text.

quote.quote: he is to deliver [his Commission and a] copy of his address to hia aid to be pre acntod to the Scorotaiy [to the President]

context_issues.problem: The piece says the reactions in the room are 'simply absent'. In fact Congress's formal answer records the institution's response and its stated emotion.

quote.quote: The United States in Congress assembled receive with emotions, too affecting for utterance

context_issues.problem: Washington's request that the officers be looked after receives a direct answer in Congress's reply. Leaving it out makes the request look unanswered.

quote.quote: will particularly charge ourselves with the interests of those confidential officers, who have attended your person to this interesting affecting moment.

context_issues.problem: The roll call is described only as 'the portion cited'. The reading range also shows Forster, Gerry and Osgood voting ay, so Partridge was the only no in the entire recorded list.

quote.quote: Mf Forster, ay Gerry, ay Osgood, ay

review.overall: Main problems: the piece cuts off before Congress's reply and wrongly says it cannot be quoted, and as a result it asserts the record shows no feeling or reaction. It also misreads 'at the request of the Member' and the bracketed revision to the protocol. Add the President's answer and correct these points before publication.
